items.headline: RBI Hikes Repo Rate by 25 Bps to 5.50%, Shifts Stance to 'Calibrated Tightening'
items.summary: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee raised the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on October 7, 2026, marking the first increase since February 2023 and signaling that controlling inflation is now its primary objective.

items.headline: India's CPI Inflation Forecast Raised to 5.2% Amid Rising Crude and Monsoon Deficit
items.summary: The RBI increased its FY2026-27 CPI inflation forecast to 5.2% from 5%, attributing the rise to re-escalating West Asia conflict pushing crude oil prices higher and a 13% deficit in the southwest monsoon impacting food prices.

items.headline: Government Boosts Domestic Defense Procurement with 'Self-Reliance' Push
items.summary: The Indian government continues its focus on self-reliance in the defense sector, with mandates for domestic procurement driving growth and opportunities for local manufacturers.

items.headline: Indian Markets Open Cautiously Despite Wall Street Gains Amid Elevated Crude Prices
items.summary: Indian equity markets opened lower today, October 27, 2026, reflecting a cautious tone influenced by persistently elevated crude oil prices (Brent crude above $100-$115 per barrel), despite overnight gains on Wall Street.

items.headline: FIIs Remain Net Sellers, DIIs Continue Buying Streak in Indian Equities
items.summary: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net sellers on October 26, offloading equities worth ₹1,462 crore, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) purchased equities worth ₹2,609 crore.

items.headline: Over 100 Companies Including L&T, Maruti Suzuki, Tata Steel to Announce Q2 FY27 Results Today
items.summary: More than 100 companies, including major players like Larsen & Toubro, Maruti Suzuki India, Bajaj Auto, Tata Steel, Cipla, and SBI Life Insurance, are scheduled to announce their Q2 FY27 financial results today.

items.headline: Paytm Reports Significant Q2 FY27 Profit Growth
items.summary: Paytm (One97 Communications) experienced significant profit growth in its Q2 FY27 results, indicating a strong financial performance for the quarter.

items.headline: Cipla's Q2 FY27 Net Profit Declines 35%, Revenue Down 2.44%
items.summary: Cipla reported a consolidated net profit decline of 35% to ₹878 crore, with revenue from operations also down 2.44% in Q2 FY27.

items.headline: ITC Hotels Posts Sharp Earnings Beat in Q2 FY27, RevPAR Up 21%
items.summary: ITC Hotels reported a sharp earnings beat in Q2 FY27, with Revenue Per Available Room (RevPAR) rising 21% and management fee income surging 25% year-on-year, and approved the incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai.

items.headline: IT Stocks Lag in Early Trade; Defense Sector in Focus
items.summary: Early trade indicated mixed sectoral performance with IT stocks (Infosys, HCL Tech) among major laggards, while the defense sector gained attention due to government procurement approvals and self-reliance initiatives.

items.headline: Tata Consumer Products Poised for 30% Upside as Key Beneficiary of Quick Commerce Growth
items.summary: Jefferies maintains a 'Buy' rating on Tata Consumer Products, expecting a 30% upside with a target price of ₹1,250, citing its position as a key beneficiary of rapid quick commerce growth.

items.headline: Vodafone Idea (VIL) Sees 34% Upside Potential Despite Target Price Reduction by Jefferies
items.summary: Jefferies has a 'Buy' rating on Vodafone Idea with a reduced target price of ₹16, still seeing a 34% upside potential and a favorable risk-reward after a recent correction.

items.headline: BSE Upgraded to 'Buy' by Motilal Oswal on Strong F&O Volume Growth Outlook
items.summary: Motilal Oswal upgraded BSE to 'Buy' with a target price of ₹4,000, anticipating strong F&O volume growth and market share expansion due to a partial CAS reversal.

content.outlook: Indian benchmark indices closed marginally lower yesterday, with the Nifty 50 down 0.21% amidst a negative market breadth of 22 advances to 36 declines. Sectoral performance was mixed, as Realty, Pharma, and Auto led gains, while Banking and IT sectors faced declines. Significant DII buying of 2610cr helped cushion the impact of FII outflows totaling 1463cr.
keyTakeaways: Nifty 50 and Sensex recorded minor losses, with overall market breadth negative.
Realty (+2.16%), Pharma (+1.76%), and Auto (+1.11%) were the top performing sectors.
Banking and IT sectors underperformed, contributing to the broader market's decline.
Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) provided strong buying support (+2610cr), counteracting Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) selling (-1463cr).
TATACONSUM (+5.7%) and DIVISLAB (+4.5%) were among the top Nifty gainers, while ADANIENT (-2.0%) and ASIANPAINT (-1.9%) were top losers.
India VIX stood at 16.705, suggesting moderate volatility.
